<reason>Side A won by forcing a clearer decision rule: outstanding identifiable duty versus irreversible consequence. PRO’s “designed absence” framing was morally vivid, but after conceding assessed lineage losses, redaction, and survivor control it either collapsed into CON’s bounded remedy or made closure impossible. A answered pressure directly and crystallized the false-choice weighing; B never specified a fulfillable endpoint that did not smuggle perpetual expansion.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s R2/closing use of B’s own “assess demonstrated losses” concession: if assessment can deny speculative inheritance/care claims, family pain can persist after the duty is discharged; if “unrepaired bloodline” overrides that, no scheme can ever close.</best_rebuttal>
